evals.prompt: /council we want to refactor our authentication middleware in the homebase monorepo. Currently every backend service has its own copy-pasted JWT verification helper (about 12 services), and we want to consolidate into a single shared library. The library will live at packages/auth-middleware/ and each service will import it. Migration must be zero-downtime, and any service that doesn't fully migrate within 2 sprints needs a fallback to keep using its old helper without compile errors. Give me a plan.
evals.expected_output: A markdown plan file that survived multiple rounds of adversarial review. Plan should include: migration strategy with sequencing, fallback mechanism for unmigrated services, verification steps (specific tests / canary deployment), risk section addressing critiques surfaced by the council (e.g., performance of shared lib at scale, test coverage gaps in the 12 services, dependency-version conflicts during the rollout window).
expectations: A markdown plan file is written to disk and its path is reported back to the user
At least 3 council subagents were spawned in parallel during at least one round (visible in the transcript)
At least 2 debate rounds were executed (or convergence early-stop documented in transcript)
The plan addresses concrete failure modes raised by council agents — not vague risks but named conditions (e.g., 'JWKS endpoint downtime causes auth failures across all 12 services simultaneously')
The plan contains a 'Verification' or equivalent section describing how to confirm the rollout worked
The plan contains a 'Risks' or 'Tradeoffs' section folding in critiques the council surfaced
Before spawning the council, the skill proposed a configuration (strategy / size / rounds) and either confirmed with the user or proceeded because the user pre-specified it

evals.prompt: /council our homebase React Native app crashes on cold start for roughly 5% of users on iOS 17 with Hermes enabled. There's no clear JS stack trace in our crash reporter (Sentry shows only a native crash without symbolicated frames). Users report it started after the 4.2.0 release. The release upgraded React Native from 0.73 to 0.85 and several native modules (react-native-mmkv, react-native-reanimated). Rank the root cause hypotheses and tell me what to investigate first.
evals.expected_output: A markdown plan that ranks at least 3 distinct root-cause hypotheses with evidence-for and evidence-against each, plus an investigation order. Plan should include specific things to check (Hermes bytecode version mismatch, MMKV migration on cold start, Reanimated worklet init on JSI, native module init order). Council should have surfaced an alternative hypothesis the user didn't mention.
expectations: A markdown plan file is written to disk and its path is reported back to the user
At least 3 distinct root-cause hypotheses are listed in the final plan
Each hypothesis is presented with evidence-for OR evidence-against AND a check that would confirm or rule it out (structured table or per-hypothesis section)
Council subagents were spawned in parallel with debugging-oriented roles (e.g., alternative-hypothesis, instrumentation, occam, prior-bug-analogue) — visible from the agent prompts in the transcript
The plan proposes a concrete next-step investigation order, not 'check everything'
At least one council round surfaced a hypothesis NOT present in the user's original prompt

evals.prompt: /council should we migrate our event ingestion pipeline from REST + Postgres to Kafka + ClickHouse? Current load is ~50k events per minute and growing roughly 2x per quarter. Postgres is starting to show contention on the events table during peak hours. Team is 4 backend engineers, 1 of whom has Kafka experience. We have a 6-month window before the projected load makes the current setup untenable.
evals.expected_output: A markdown plan that takes a clear position (migrate / don't migrate / phased) and defends it against multi-perspective critique. Plan should include: complexity-budget honest accounting, alternative considered (e.g., Postgres partitioning, columnar extension), staffing realism for Kafka operation, and a phased migration approach with rollback path. The plan should NOT just say 'yes migrate to Kafka' uncritically.
expectations: A markdown plan file is written to disk and its path is reported back to the user
The plan takes a clear recommended position rather than listing options without choosing
The plan considers and explicitly addresses at least one alternative to the proposed Kafka + ClickHouse move (e.g., Postgres partitioning, write-side sharding, TimescaleDB)
Complexity-budget concerns are explicitly addressed (operational toil, team size relative to system count)
The plan includes a phased migration plan with a rollback path, not just a big-bang switch
Council subagents were spawned (or simulated inline if Agent tool unavailable) with architecture-oriented roles (e.g., scalability, complexity-budget, vendor-lock-in, evolvability)
At least 2 debate rounds executed by default, with severity-weighted early-stop allowed
